title: GOV-0060: BADF-WP-GIT-G — recovery: `git-recovery` inventories unique state and classifies the recovery path (read-only), `--preserve` adds recovery refs and touches nothing else; git-recovery subskill
problem:
## Observed

`badf-git`'s recovery contract (`references/recovery-contract.md`) opens with one rule — `PRESERVE → IDENTIFY → CLASSIFY → RECOVER → VERIFY → RECONCILE`; "never start with `reset --hard`, destructive `clean`, forced protected-ref movement, or deletion of unknown branches/worktrees merely because the repository is inconvenient" — and says that when state is unknown, recovery **stops mutation until it is classified**, listing the ten questions to answer first (which worktree, which ref, what is HEAD, what is staged/unstaged/untracked, which commits exist only locally, what is authoritative, is any content the only copy, is another actor relying on the branch/worktree, what authority covers the recovery, which evidence goes stale). `GIT-O5` requires "inventory/preservation of unique state" and "evidence of the before state" before any exception. Measured after GIT-F: **nothing produces that inventory, nothing preserves anything, and the recovery trigger GIT-F introduced — a `BLOCKED` reconcile — ends with the words "open recovery" and no tooling behind them.** In this program the "preservation" practised so far was a hand-typed `git branch backup/...` before every rebase; the `test_badf_integrity` residue that blocked a rebase earlier today was exactly unclassified unique state met with a hand-run `git checkout --`. GTGM v0.1 §12 (reverse/rollback/recovery contract), §15 (`git-recovery` subskill), §17 **GIT-G — Recovery**.

## Expected

**Preservation and classification become measured records; nothing destructive is added.**

1. **`badf_gate.py git-recovery [<path>]`** (read-only, `GIT-O0`) renders one JSON **git-recovery record** — the before-state evidence the contract requires: the `git-baseline` identity (reused: worktree, HEAD, target, ahead/behind, counts) plus the **unique-state inventory**: uncommitted changes (counts only), stash entries, **dangling commits** (reflog entries of HEAD unreachable from any ref — the only copy of a commit), **unpushed topic commits** (local branches ahead of their upstream, or with none), and **other worktrees** of the same repository with the branch each holds (another actor may be relying on it). From that it derives the contract's **recovery class** — `EVIDENCE_ONLY` (nothing unique; only records may be stale), `LOCAL` (unique uncommitted/stashed/dangling state), `TOPIC` (unpushed commits), `PROTECTED` (HEAD is the default branch, or the target moved past the recorded base) — and a **disposition**: `RECOVERABLE` (unique state exists and can be preserved), `RECOVERY_REQUIRED` (unique state exists **and** a preservation would be needed before any destructive step), `BLOCKED` (state cannot be classified: not a repository, unborn HEAD, unmerged paths). It prints the **least-destructive path** as text (preserve → then the class's recipe). Deterministic modulo `observed_at`; counts only, never a path or content.
2. **`badf_gate.py git-recovery --preserve <label> --wp <WP> [<path>]`** (`GIT-O1`, opt-in) establishes preservation the only way that cannot lose anything: `refs/recovery/<WP>/<label>` at HEAD, and — when the worktree/index is dirty — `refs/recovery/<WP>/<label>-worktree` at a commit produced by `git stash create` (which writes objects and **touches neither the worktree, the index nor the stash list**). It refuses to overwrite an existing recovery ref of the same label, refuses without `--wp`, and never runs `reset`, `clean`, `checkout` or any ref *deletion*. The record then carries `preservation: {refs, before_head, worktree_snapshot}` — the contract's "preservation step".
3. **The revert pattern for landed work stays a procedure**, not code: the `git-recovery` subskill (GTGM §15) maps the six stages to commands — inventory, preserve, classify, then per class: reflog → recovery ref → verify (local); `--force-with-lease` only on a private topic after preservation (topic); **a new recovery WP with a `git revert` composed against current `main`** (protected — the `BLOCKED`-reconcile path from GIT-F); tags never rewritten (release, GIT-H). Registered `IMPLEMENTED`, C1, `allowed_tools: []`; the `badf-git` root stays `DESIGNED`.
4. **CI positive control:** the runner renders its own recovery record (`EVIDENCE_ONLY` on a clean checkout).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Clean checkout at the target → class `EVIDENCE_ONLY`, disposition `RECOVERABLE`, every unique-state count zero, no dangling commits, no unpushed commits.
2. Uncommitted and stashed changes → class `LOCAL`, disposition `RECOVERY_REQUIRED`, counts reported **without paths or contents**.
3. A commit made then `reset --hard` away → reported as a **dangling commit** (reflog-only), `LOCAL`, `RECOVERY_REQUIRED`; the path text names the reflog → recovery-ref recipe.
4. A topic branch with commits not on any upstream → `TOPIC`; HEAD on the default branch → `PROTECTED`.
5. A second (linked) worktree of the same repository → listed with its branch; the record never reports the caller's own worktree as "another".
6. `--preserve` on a dirty tree → creates exactly the two refs, HEAD unchanged, index digest unchanged, `git status` unchanged, stash list unchanged; on a clean tree → one ref; an existing label → refused; missing `--wp` → usage error; the preserved worktree ref's tree equals the dirty tree's content (verified by checking it out in a scratch clone).
7. Refusals (`BLOCKED`): outside a repository; unborn HEAD; unmerged paths present (classification impossible until conflicts are resolved).
8. Read-only proven for the inventory (status/reflog/stash/index/refs byte-identical); deterministic modulo `observed_at`; each classification and refusal branch **load-bearing** (mutation).
9. `git-recovery` subskill registered `IMPLEMENTED` C1 `allowed_tools: []` with a real digest; root stays `DESIGNED`; no new script, no schema, no authority change; `repo` clean; full suite + compose green in CI; the runner's own record renders.

## Tests (`tests/test_badf_git_recovery.py`, scratch clones via `tests/_scratch.seed_clone`)

- `test_clean_checkout_is_EVIDENCE_ONLY_and_RECOVERABLE`
- `test_uncommitted_and_stash_are_LOCAL_RECOVERY_REQUIRED_without_paths`
- `test_dangling_reflog_commit_is_inventoried`
- `test_unpushed_topic_commits_are_TOPIC`
- `test_head_on_default_branch_is_PROTECTED`
- `test_other_worktrees_are_listed_but_not_self`
- `test_preserve_adds_refs_and_touches_nothing_else`
- `test_preserve_refuses_existing_label_and_requires_wp`
- `test_refusals_outside_repo_unborn_head_and_unmerged_paths`
- `test_inventory_is_read_only_and_deterministic`
- `test_git_recovery_subskill_registered_and_root_stays_designed`

## Out of scope

- Any destructive operation (`reset --hard`, `clean`, forced ref moves, branch/worktree deletion, tag rewrites) — the tool never performs them; it makes them safe to *consider*.
- Executing a revert or opening the recovery WP — a human/agent action under a new work package (the procedure).
- Release-ref recovery — **GIT-H**; `rerere` policy beyond what `commit-integrity` already states; the remote-workspace mode (#133).

## Risk / authority / stop conditions

- Change class **C1** (read-only inventory; opt-in ref *creation* only). Target gate **G07**, `HUMAN_REQUIRED`.
- Stop if preservation would require anything beyond creating refs, if classification would need network, or if scope grows past one subcommand (two modes) + one subskill + tests + doctrine.
- Lean mode: **enforced** — reuse `git_baseline`, `_git_at`, the scratch fixture; `git stash create` + `update-ref` as the entire preservation mechanism.

## Identity

- Ledger **WP-2026-0080** · demand **BADF-DEM-0067** · this issue **GOV-0060** · phase label BADF-WP-GIT-G. Ids measured across `main`, every remote branch head and all issues.
- Branch `wp/WP-2026-0080-git-recovery` in a linked worktree from `928fc6b`; reconciles whatever is `LANDED_UNRECONCILED` at branch time (WP-2026-0079 now — already verified `composition_verified: true`).
- Sequence: A ✓ B ✓ C ✓ D ✓ E ✓ F ✓ → **G (this)** → H → I → J.
